title: Who Turns Milk Into Curd? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya leaves warm milk with a spoon of curd on the kitchen shelf, and by morning it is thick and sour. The same tiny group lives in hot springs and turns dirty ponds green. Meet the bacteria, the only members of kingdom Monera.

A zoom ladder goes from a bowl of curd to one drop to a typical bacterium, labelled: cell wall, cell membrane, loose DNA with no nuclear membrane, ribosomes and flagellum. You will see the four shapes (cocci, bacilli, vibrio, spirilla), archaebacteria (halophiles, thermoacidophiles, methanogens and biogas) against eubacteria, cyanobacteria with chlorophyll a and nitrogen-fixing heterocysts in Nostoc and Anabaena, chemosynthetic and heterotrophic bacteria, fission running live, spores, DNA transfer and Mycoplasma. Then a worked sort of six bacteria, the blue green algae exam trap, an original NEET pattern assertion and reason question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 13 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
